samples.evidence: The same "walk up blockParentMap with a `seen` Set" loop now exists at `table-layout.ts:487` (`resolveNestedTableLayout`), `text-editor.ts:3894` (`findOuterCellAddress`), `text-editor.ts:3919` (`findOutermostTableId`), and — added by this delta — `selection.ts:127` (`walkToTopLevelBlockId`) and inline in `peer-cursor.ts:118-136`. samples.summary: Nested-table doc still says no hierarchy-path helper is needed and records nothing about the render-path resolver contract this PR establishes
samples.evidence: `docs-nested-tables.md:163-167` states "No dedicated hierarchy-path helper is needed — structural operations only need the direct parent". This PR series establishes the opposite for the view layer: `resolveNestedTableLayout` is now the mandatory nested-aware lookup for painting, shift+click, clipboard copy and peer cursors, plus a cycle-bounded parent-chain walk that every consumer must carry. The canonical subsystem doc records none of that, so the next contributor reading it will reach for the flat `layout.blocks.find` that caused #1049. This is a doc-currency gap on a behavior-only bugfix, not an architecture change, so it does not block.

samples.summary: resolvePositionPixel reimplements the whole nested-table descent that resolveNestedTableLayout already performs; the delta patches the copy instead of reusing the resolver
samples.evidence: `peer-cursor.ts:114-200` builds a `nestingPath`, finds the top-level `layoutTable`, and descends accumulating `xOffset`/`yOffset` — the same job `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts:474-590) does and returns as `{layoutTable, dataBlock, xOffset, yOffset}`. The rest of the PR converged selection.ts and text-editor.ts onto the resolver; this delta instead hand-copies the resolver's cycle guard into the peer-cursor copy, entrenching the second implementation. Two independent descents over the same nesting geometry are two answers to one question, and the offsets they compute must stay in agreement for remote carets to land where the selection paints.
